title: Residue recovery from the normalized quotient homotopy limit
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative Noetherian ring, $J$ an ideal, and $U$ an object of the coefficient-sized pro-etale site. Write $R$ for the completed coefficient ring sheaf on the slice, $q_n:R\to B_n$ for its actual projections, and $F_n=-\otimes_R^L B_n$, $G_n$ for the specified scalar restriction [def-sfb-adic-residue-lift-comparisons]. For $M\in D(R)$ use the normalized adjunctions $F_n\dashv G_n$ and their counit-transpose tower $T_n=G_nF_nM$ [lem-sfb-adic-residue-adjoint-tower]. Let $c$ be any Roos homotopy-limit cone over this tower [def-weil-derived-limit]. The adjoint transpose $p:F_0(c.pt)\to F_0M$ of its leg $c_0:c.pt\to G_0F_0M$ is an isomorphism. No completeness or boundedness of $M$, no map $M\to c.pt$, and no perfectness of $B_0$ over $R$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion, Koszul/quotient comparison; Tag 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion-koszul, with the prescribed degree-zero unit. The finite-reduction consequence is obtained by the reflector Hom bijection and scalar adjunction, not by commuting tensor with arbitrary products.

proof.text: Choose a single flat-term K-flat representative P of M. Apply the strict augmentation calculation to obtain an actual quotient tensor tower T, an augmentation alpha from the negative Koszul tensor tower with pro-zero cone, and a normalized levelwise isomorphism to the counit-transpose adjoint tower. The strict-tower theorem inverts Q(alpha) under total right derived inverse limit. Uniqueness of total right derived functors transfers this assertion to the inverse limit in the chosen Koszul presentation. Construct its Roos cone using the strict-tower proof and check that the comparison with ordinary inverse limit preserves each projection.

Use the general ringed-site companion ringedKoszulCompletionReflector, retained in Sheaf.CategoryTheory.RingedKoszulCompletionReflector, on the completed slice kernel generated by the completed images. Every finite-coefficient restriction is complete: powers of each generator act by zero, its localization vanishes, and complete elements form the generated ideal. For any residue complex N the reflector mapping bijection into G_0 N, conjugated by F_0 dashv G_0, makes the image of the reflector unit bijective on all outgoing Hom sets. Coyoneda makes this image invertible.

Descend the natural complex-level Koszul unit through localization, so unitOnComplex P is the reflector unit at Q(P). The isomorphism induced by alpha, the tensorFactors isomorphism, and the isomorphism from the normalized strict Roos cone to the supplied cone give g:Q(P)->c.pt. The ordinary-limit projection calculation and the augmentation normalization show g followed by the nth leg equals the representative isomorphism eP followed by the nth scalar unit. At n=0, transposition says F_0(g) followed by p equals F_0(eP). The first factor is invertible by the reflector finite-unit argument, and the right side is invertible. Cancellation therefore proves IsIso(p). The unit naturality uses the already stated Cech/Koszul colimit and ordinary-limit comparisons, not any uniqueness of normalized maps to arbitrary quotient cones.

theorem adicResidue_quotient_residue_projection_isIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) {A : Type (max v (u + 1))} [CommRing A] [IsNoetherianRing A]
    (J : Ideal A) (U : coefficientProEtaleSiteModel.{u, v} X)
    (M : AdicResidueLocalDerived.{u, v} X J U)
    (c : Cone (adicResidueAdjointTower.{u, v} X J U M))
    (hc : Pretriangulated.IsHomotopyLimit c) :
    IsIso (((adicResidueScalarAdjunction.{u, v} X J U 0).homEquiv c.pt
      ((adicResidueLocalReduction.{u, v} X J U 0).obj M)).symm
        (c.π.app (op 0)))
